claim: For independent original coordinates with density caps one, after an orthogonal spectral change of coordinates the selected three spectral coordinates have a universally bounded conditional density given the complementary spectral coordinates.
counterexample: Take X_1,...,X_4 iid Uniform[0,1], u=(1,1,1,1)/2, choose r_1,r_2,r_3 an orthonormal basis of u^perp and r_4=u. With Y=R^T X, Y_4=(sum X_i)/2. For 0<w<1/2, f_{Y_4}(w)=2 f_{sum X_i}(2w)=(8/3)w^3. The joint Y-density is the indicator of a rotated unit cube, so the conditional density of (Y_1,Y_2,Y_3) given Y_4=w is constant on the section with essential supremum 1/f_{Y_4}(w)=3/(8w^3), which diverges as w downarrow0. Taking A=R diag(1,1,-1,0) R^T puts the construction inside the exact three-large-eigenvalue spectral setup.
scope_warning: This is not a counterexample to QFORM-DENSITY. It refutes only the conditional spectral-projection density bridge proposed in owner revision 2026-09-22.8. A successful rank-three route must retain product provenance before or jointly with the indefinite curved trace.
